title: Bound the executor handoff, and the multiplier behind it (gh-464, gh-461)
body:
Closes #464. Closes #461.

**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-20-bounded-executor-handoff-design.md`
**Plan:** `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-20-bounded-executor-handoff/` (5 phases, all complete)

## What this is not

Most of what #464 asked for **already shipped** in 4.2.0 (PR #465): `fr journal handoff`, fr-plan's "prefer 4–6 phases" guidance, the nested per-phase review loop, the skeleton mandate, refactor-or-justify, V1 context accounting, and #461's return-only reporting rule. All six `goal-*` acceptance rows were already at `ci`.

Nothing here rebuilds any of it. This PR fixes what **measuring #465's own output** revealed.

## The measurement

Against the real archived journal for `2026-09-18-harness-parity-matrix` (729 lines, 130k chars), the shipped handoff was a discount, not a bound:

| phase | before | after | cut |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 35,080 | **26,593** | −24.2% |
| 2 | 47,028 | **32,838** | −30.2% |
| 3 | 46,889 | **30,328** | −35.3% |
| 4 | 50,439 | **34,404** | −31.8% |
| 5 | 66,228 | **39,694** | −40.1% |
| 6 | 83,132 | **49,110** | −40.9% |
| 7 | 68,908 | **49,874** | −27.6% |

Growth across six phases fell from **2.4× to 1.85×**.

Two categories never reached `compose_handoff`'s collapse branch: **untagged entries**, which render in full at every phase forever (the `no-refactor-because` bookkeeping #465's own gate manufactures), and **fixed findings tagged to a dependency phase** — and real plans depend on their predecessors, so the rule rarely fired.

### The spec's prediction was wrong, and by how much is recorded

§5.A3 predicted ~46k at phase 6 and ~24k at phase 1. Reality: 49,110 and 26,593 — consistently ~6% optimistic. The cause is measured, not guessed: 16 untagged entries (13,281 chars) still render in full at phase 6, because the residual table assumed that bookkeeping was phase-*tagged*. That is §5.A2's residual, which phase 3 addresses **for new writes only** — it does not shrink journals already on disk, and the PR does not claim it does.

## What shipped

**Pillar 1 — the bound**
- `compose_handoff` consults an entry's **effective state** before its phase: a closed finding or resolution record collapses to one line regardless of dependency. Decisions and discoveries keep dependency scoping deliberately — they carry forward value.
- A re-opening resolution record is the one exception and renders in full; collapsing it dropped the only text saying why a finding was live again.
- `fr journal add --scope plan` now requires `--phase N` **or** `--global`. Neither is an error naming the consequence.

**Pillar 2 — the multiplier**
- A sixth executor-contract norm (context discipline), landed in **both** contract files — `fr-phase-executor.md` for Claude Code and OpenCode, and `fr-execute` for Hermes, which has no agent mirror.
- `fr.run.telemetry`: a Claude Code transcript reader, four optional `PhaseAccounting` token fields, the `run` artifact stamp bump 2→3 with a registered migration and validator, and `fr run status` rendering where measured and estimated are distinguishable.

## Verification

Full gate on a **macOS host**, after merging `origin/main` (`4fc5421`):

```
pytest                3423 passed, 80 skipped, 3 failed
ruff check            All checks passed
ruff format --check   373 files already formatted
mypy (4 src trees)    Success: no issues found in 141 source files
bump-version --check  ok — versions agree (4.10.0)
fr acceptance check   135 rows OK (ci 113 / skipped 18 / not-implemented 4)
fr validate artifacts 33 artifact(s) checked — all structurally valid
fr workflow check     fr-goal: ok
sync-opencode/hermes  both in sync
fr journal check      clean (exit 0)
fr plan self-review   passed
bun test (opencode)   15 pass, 0 fail
```

**GitHub CI is green on every job** (lint, matrix, test, typecheck,
validate-artifacts, version-sync, version-bump-required, opencode-plugin-test).

The 3 failures are exactly the known #489 macOS-only set (two `test_run_workspace.py` marker refusals, one non-hermetic `test_workflow_check.py::test_cli_all_fails_when_nothing_is_discoverable`). **Stated precisely because it is environment-dependent:** phase 5's executor reported "0 failed" truthfully from inside a devcontainer, where those three do not fire. Neither number is wrong; the host picture is 3 known / 0 new.

### The telemetry measured itself

The strongest evidence in the PR: the live run cursor for *this run* recorded `phase/4/implement-phase: cache-read 24865760, out 96435`, byte-identical to an independent probe of that agent's transcript. #464's scar — a parser and its fixtures written from the same guess — is not reproduced.

## Findings and fixes

25 findings across five per-phase reviews, all resolved (`fr journal check` clean). Full text: `fr journal render --scope plan --slug 2026-09-20-bounded-executor-handoff --section findings`.

The ones worth a reviewer's time:

| id | finding |
|---|---|
| `r1-c1` | **Privacy leak** — the leak test asserted absence by *listing* an operator username and two third-party org names, in a public repo. The branch was unpushed, so the commit was amended rather than fixed forward; no commit in `origin/main..HEAD` contains the strings. |
| `r1-c2` | The transcript fixture merged two streams into a **file shape the harness never emits**, and a green test pinned the assumption phase 1 had just disproved — with phase 4 pointed at it. |
| `r1-c3` | A phase reported its gate green while `ruff format --check` was red. `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` are not interchangeable. |
| `r2-i1` | **Regression introduced by this PR:** a re-opening resolution record collapsed. No test covered it — applying the fix left all 92 green. The spec said "or a resolution record, collapses", so the blind spot was upstream. |
| `r3-i1` | The flagship test passed **only at 80 columns** — it matched rich's soft-wrapped output. |
| `r3-i3` | An acceptance row flipped to `ci` claiming prose coverage no test provided. |
| `r3-i4` | An assertion proved vacuous: replacing the entire message with `"nope"` left all 40 tests green. |
| `r4-i1` | The telemetry reader was **locale-dependent and failed silently** — under `LC_ALL=C` it returned `None`, indistinguishable from "no transcript". Reproduced on a real transcript. |
| `r4-i2` | The estimate and the measurement differ by **~1,426×** on this run's own cursor because they count different things; labelling them differently was not enough. |
| `r5-i1` | A journal decision quoted a "plan carve-out" that **exists in no committed artifact** — it came from a dispatch brief. Headed verbatim into this PR body. Corrected by appending. |
| `r5-i2` | The version rationale's premise was **false on disk** (38 of 47 archived plans carry `<4.0.0` and are not stranded). The verdict survives on better reasons — see below. |
| `r5-i3` | The new norm reached **two harnesses of three**; Hermes has no agent mirror. The acceptance sentence said "every harness that mirrors the agent" — true, and quietly narrowing. |

## Operator gates

```
brainstorm: operator gate answered by the operator
```

One gate, one batched Q&A, four decisions (d1–d4), recorded as spec-scope journal entries.

## Version: 4.10.0 (minor) — your call to overrule

`fr journal add --scope plan` now **requires** a flag it previously did not, which breaks any existing caller. By AGENTS.md's ladder that reads as a breaking CLI change.

Shipped as **minor** anyway, for reasons the phase-5 review corrected and I accept:

1. AGENTS.md names this case under Minor explicitly — *"user-visible workflow additions (new subcommand/skill/**mandatory behavior**)"*.
2. Every caller of the newly-strict flag ships **in this PR**; `fr` is not published as a library.
3. No plan-schema break and no interface a consumer repo holds.

The originally-recorded reason — "major would strand every plan's `<5.0.0` ceiling" — was **wrong**, and is corrected in the journal rather than quietly dropped. If you prefer 5.0.0 on strict-semver grounds the cost is bounded: a registered `<5.0.0` → `<6.0.0` migration for the five live plans, in this PR.

### Why 4.10.0 and not 4.9.0

This branch originally chose 4.9.0. While it ran, `main` published 4.9.0 too. **Git reported no conflict**, because both sides had written the identical string — but two different contents under one version is exactly the installer-caching trap AGENTS.md warns about, and a three-way merge cannot see it. Caught by comparing `main`'s manifest rather than trusting the clean merge.

## Test Plan (post-merge — operator-driven)

1. Run a small real `/fr-goal` (3 phases) and confirm `fr run status` reports **measured** Claude Code token figures per phase, not estimates.
2. Compare that run's per-phase handoff sizes against the before-figures in §2, and report the A4 residual (`norefactor-*` entries in dependency phases).
3. Confirm the two follow-up issues exist and are accurate.

## Acceptance

Four rows added at brainstorm, all now `ci`:

| row | defense |
|---|---|
| `handoff-closed-entries-bounded` | A closed entry costs O(1) chars regardless of body size — the property that is true. Non-monotonic growth was **refuted** in spec review and never claimed. |
| `handoff-entries-always-tagged` | Writing a plan-scope entry forces an explicit phase-or-global choice; all four refusal paths pinned. |
| `executor-context-discipline` | The norm is present in the canonical agent, all four OpenCode mirrors, and (after `r5-i3`) `fr-execute`, which all three harnesses mirror. |
| `run-telemetry-measured-claude-code` | Fixtures are captures with a provenance note; both halves pinned, including a measured zero and an unreadable transcript. |

Repo debt unchanged at **18 skipped / 4 not-implemented** — none introduced here.

## Follow-ups filed

- **#509** — V2 transcript telemetry for OpenCode and Hermes (carries the real Claude Code shape and states the unknowns as unknowns).
- **#510** — investigate importing `derio-net/agnostic-fr` harness-conformance testing.
- **#511** — capture or refute a Claude Code assistant record with no `message.usage`; the close-path for phase 4's one open finding, which was resolved citing it rather than downgraded to green a gate.

## Known gaps, stated rather than implied

- **Phase 3 fixes new writes, not old journals.** The ~6% residual persists in journals already on disk.
- **The A4 residual is real**: `no-refactor-because` entries tagged to a *dependency* phase still render in full. Named in the spec, not hidden by the 40% figure.
- **`docs/explainers/01-fr-goal.md` was not regenerated** — checked against every behaviour change in this PR and no sentence is made false, so nothing is owed. (Pre-existing, not newly false: line 401 says the executor gets "the running journal" when it gets a curated handoff — drifted in #465.)
- **Pre-existing privacy debt, out of scope:** `docs/superpowers/implemented/journals/plans/2026-09-18-harness-parity-matrix.md`, already on `main`, contains the operator's real username. Archived artifacts are frozen by rule, so this PR does not touch it.

## Merged `origin/main` (#506, #507, #512, #515)

Eight files conflicted; **three were sources**, five were generated and were regenerated by their own scripts rather than hand-merged.

- **`AGENTS.md`** — `main` had *independently* added the same `sync-hermes.py` documentation this PR's phase 3 added, from gh#434 phase 5, which hit the identical trap. Took `main`'s: it cites the issue and the discovery. Two PRs finding the same gap in one week is evidence the trap was real.
- **`fr-goal/SKILL.md`** — both rewrote one sentence for unrelated reasons (this PR: the `--phase N` example and the return-only rule; `main`: `resolved_tier` resolution). Kept both, still exactly 120 lines.
- **`matrix.yaml`** — disjoint row additions (4 here, 7 there, no id overlap). Kept all eleven.

---

## Ready checklist — do not merge until all three hold

- [ ] CI green on this branch
- [ ] Explicit review OK from the operator
- [ ] No commits pushed since that OK

This PR is a **draft** and stays one until the boxes are checked. Not self-merged.
